'''Sergio Fubini''' (31 December 1928 – 6 January 2005) was an [[Italians|Italian]] theoretical physicist. He was one of the pioneers of [[string theory]]. He was engaged in peace activism in the [[Middle East]].<ref>Vittorio de Alfaro e Giuseppe Furlan, ''Commemorazione di Sergio Fubini'', Acc. Sc. Torino – Atti Ufficiali, (2004-2006), 103-121.</ref>

== Biography ==
Fubini was born in [[Turin]]. In 1938, he fled the country as a politically persecuted Jew to [[Switzerland]]. In 1945, he attended the Lycée in Turin, where he studied physics and in 1950 graduated "cum laude." Afterwards, he was an assistant in Turin. From 1954 to 1957, he was in the USA. From 1958 to 1967, he was at [[CERN]] in [[Geneva]]. In 1959, he became a professor of nuclear physics at [[University of Padua]]. In 1961, he became a professor of theoretical physics at [[University of Turin]]. From 1968 to 1973, he was at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], but taught summer courses in Turin. He went back to CERN in 1973 and was from 1971 to 1980 a member of the advisory board and had an important role in planning the [[Large Electron Positron Collider]] (LEP) as well as in discussions for the construction of the Middle East's Synchrotron, [[International Centre for Synchrotron-Light for Experimental Science Applications in the Middle East|SESAME]].<ref>{{Citation |last1=Schopper |first1=Herwig |chapter=Science for Peace with SESAME and SEEIIST |date=2024 |title=Herwig Schopper |pages=215–240 |place=Cham |publisher=Springer International Publishing |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-51042-7_11 |isbn=978-3-031-51041-0 |last2=Gillies |first2=James|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Schopper|first1=Herwig|title=SESAME: a mini-CERN for the Middle East|journal=CERN Courier|date=March 2000|volume=40|issue=2|pages=17–18|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733042}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Llewellyn Smith|first1=Chris|title=Viewpoint: A shining light in the Middle East|journal=CERN Courier|date=September 2014|volume=54|issue=7|page=46|url=http://iopp.fileburst.com/ccr/archive/CERNCourier2014Sep-digitaledition.pdf|access-date=2015-04-01|archive-date=2020-09-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923152956/http://iopp.fileburst.com/ccr/archive/CERNCourier2014Sep-digitaledition.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At MIT, he was with [[Gabriele Veneziano]], [[Emilio Del Giudice]] and [[Paolo Di Vecchia]] at the centre of an active school of theoretical physicists with close connections to Italy (with one of the Italian [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare|INFN]] and MIT financed "Bruno Rossi" exchange programs). He and his co-workers did fundamental work in [[string theory]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?isbn=0521197902 The Birth of String Theory]</ref> Other well-known MIT colleagues at that time were [[Victor Weisskopf]] (who was recruited by Fubini to MIT), [[Steven Weinberg]] and [[Roman Jackiw]]. From 1994 to 2001, he was a professor in Turin. Fubini worked in the 1960s on [[current algebra]]s and [[S-matrix theory]] ([[Regge theory|Regge trajectories]] among other things), in particular on their field-theoretical foundations. In the 1970s, he was with his MIT colleagues and pupils Gabriele Veneziano, Emilio Del Giudice and Paolo Di Vecchia one of the pioneers of [[string theory]] (the team introduced the so-called [[DDF states]]).<ref>{{cite journal|title=General properties of the dual resonances model|author=Emilio Del Giudice |author2=Paolo Di Vecchia|author3=Sergio Fubini|journal=Annals of Physics |pages=378–398 |date=1972|doi=10.1016/0003-4916(72)90272-2|volume=70|issue=2|bibcode = 1972AnPhy..70..378D }}</ref> He worked in the 1970s on other classical solutions of [[Yang–Mills theory|Yang–Mills equations]] and conformally invariant quantum field theory.<ref>{{cite journal|title=New Approaches to Field Theory|author=Fubini, S.|author2=Hanson, A. J.|author3=Jackiw, R.|journal=Phys. Rev. D |pages=1732–1760|date=1973|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.7.1732|volume=7|issue=6|bibcode = 1973PhRvD...7.1732F }}</ref>

Fubini died in 2005 in [[Nyon]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=People: Sergio Fubini 1928-2005|journal=CERN Courier|date=March 2005|volume=45|issue=2|page=39|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733745}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Khan|first1=Sameen Ahmed|title=People: Sergio Fubini, MESC and SESAME|journal=CERN Courier|date=May 2005|volume=45|issue=4|page=44|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1733773}}</ref> He married Marina Colombo in 1956 and had a daughter with her.

== Honors ==
Fubini received the [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]] in 1968 and received an honorary doctorate from the [[University of Heidelberg]].
